sentences.text: Phosphorosaurus was an extinct marine lizard belonging to the mosasaur family.
This animal was relatively small, reaching lengths of only 3 to 4 meters compared to many other mosasaurs.
The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, consists of a fragmented skull estimated to be around 42 cm long.
Large eyes with overlapping fields of vision provided depth perception for hunting in low light.
The name P. ponpetelegans honors the clean Pankerusano-sawa Creek in Hokkaido where the exceptionally preserved holotype was found.
The genus Phosphorosaurus was first described by Louis Dollo in 1889.
Louis Dollo defined the genus in 1889 based on fossils from the upper Maastrichtian Craie phosphateé of Ciply in Belgium.
Analysis suggests Phosphorosaurus was a deep-water or nocturnal hunter that likely preyed on squid and bioluminescent fish.
Phosphorosaurus belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
The parent group of Phosphorosaurus is Halisaurini.
It belongs to the Halisaurinae subfamily of mosasaurs.
Although often treated as a synonym of Halisaurus, a 2015 study recognizes Phosphorosaurus as a valid genus.
The species was reclassified as Halisaurus ortliebi in 1996, but later authorities rejected this due to cranial differences.
Phosphorosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
Phosphorosaurus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
Two species of Phosphorosaurus are known: P. ortliebi from Belgium and P. ponpetelegans from Japan.
P. ponpetelegans lived only in the earliest Maastrichtian, while P. ortliebi lived throughout the Maastrichtian.
Some researchers suggest Phosphorosaurus ponpetelegans might represent a distinct genus that needs a new name rather than being part of Halisaurus.
